text: There are answers. Keep the distances between midfield and defence tight. Pressure the passer before the run starts. Pass runners between defenders instead of chasing them blindly. And when Barcelona commit players forward, use the space they leave on a turnover. Sevilla's first half showed that this team can be disrupted. The experiment still has to survive fatigue, tighter opponents and days when the finishing stops looking effortless. But that is what makes it worth watching. Raphinha is giving Barcelona more ways to punish the same defensive hesitation. Whether this breaks La Liga will be decided over the season. Right now, though, Flick has put an exceptional mover where one step can change a match. So when the next centre-back checks over his shoulder, the question is simple. Does he follow Raphinha, or protect the space Raphinha is about to attack?
